notes: Every dough amount is a baker's percentage of flour weight (flour = 100%).
Values are objects: value (or range), confidence (high/medium/low), verified (true only when checked against a primary source by a person), sources (URLs), optional note.
No recipe has been test-baked yet. verified is false everywhere on purpose.
Sizes in 'sizes' (round 26, 30 and 32 cm) are the ones the site offers. Dough per pizza = round area x style.dough_density_g_per_cm2 (styles new_york and neapolitan).
Validation review 2026-11: values changed after an independent review are noted in their 'note' fields; none was test-baked. See docs/test-bake-plan.md.

max_c.note: Home oven up to 250 degrees (user's setup).

oven.mode_note: Top and bottom heat, no fan.

preheat_min.note: Preheat the baking surface 45-60 minutes. From the user's guide; the cast-iron tray heat-up time was not measured.

surface.note: Pizza stone, baking steel or cast-iron pan are all fine. Steel and cast iron conduct heat better than stone (America's Test Kitchen). Cast-iron advice is home-tested only; no controlled test was found.

mode_info.note: Validation review 2026-11 (m1): the guide keeps top and bottom heat with no fan. Reason: in plain fan mode the bottom element is often off, so the base gets less heat, and moving air dries and browns the top faster. Oven makers recommend a pizza mode (fan plus bottom heat); the site mentions it as an option to try. Advice varies by oven. The earlier reason ('the fan burns the top before the base is ready') was overstated.

shape_lead_min.note: Open the dough about 15 minutes before it goes in the oven; open it only when the oven is ready (second pizza waits as a ball, not on the paper).

fresh_to_dry.note: Fresh yeast = 3x instant dry yeast (King Arthur Baker's Hotline, quoted in a Fresh Loaf thread). Active dry is often quoted as 2-2.5x; Common dry yeast packets are instant.

source_spread_x.note: Yeast amounts for the same schedule differ up to 5x between sources.

solution_threshold_dry_g.note: Design rule: use the yeast solution when the dry-equivalent yeast is under 1.5 g, otherwise weigh the yeast directly. The user's scale reads whole grams only.

yeast_g.note: One whole common 7 g packet of instant dry yeast.
Half of a common 42 g cube of fresh yeast.

cube_g.note: Common fresh yeast cube size; check your pack.

solution.note: Use immediately. A shelf life for a diluted yeast solution was not found in any source, so none is stated. Yeast dissolved in water loses vigour with time (secondhand source). Stir again right before weighing out the amount, because the yeast settles (validation M6).

water_temp_c.note: Validation review 2026-11 (M6): lukewarm water for the yeast solution, given as a number. The user's guide said only 'lukewarm'. Well below the about 50 C where yeast starts to die.

dissolve_wait_min.note: Validation review 2026-11 (M6): stir until no lumps are left, wait about 5 minutes for dry yeast to dissolve, then stir again right before pouring out the amount; yeast settles within minutes. Food-science reasoning, no source. See docs/test-bake-plan.md, item 5.

notes: Common 7 g packets are instant yeast: they can be mixed straight into the flour and need no proofing (retailer descriptions; the official oetker.de page was not reachable). Check the packet text.
A 7 g packet is meant for about 500 g flour (1.4%); this guide uses much less per dough for fridge methods.

parchment_max_c.note: Common baking paper is rated to 220 C. Not advised with the grill function or touching oven walls. Some premium papers are rated 240-250 C; check the pack. Not wax paper (it is not made for the oven). If the paper is rated below the oven temperature, pull it out after the first 2-3 minutes (validation m8).

evoo_smoke_c.note: Extra-virgin olive oil smokes around 190-210 C (industry sites; UC Davis notes smoke point alone does not predict quality loss). At 250 C use refined olive oil or a neutral oil (rapeseed, sunflower) in pans. Oil mixed into the dough is fine. The recipe pages brush a thin film of olive oil on the rim before baking (the original guide's advice); a refined or light olive oil resists smoke better.

parchment_pull_min.note: Validation review 2026-11 (m8): if the paper is rated below the oven temperature, pull it out from under the pizza after the first 2-3 minutes, when the base has set. Practice advice, untested. See docs/test-bake-plan.md, item 6.

measures.note: Approximate household measures for the 'About' column next to the grams. Grams stay the exact main unit; this column is the only rounded output. Level measuring spoons, 5 ml teaspoon, 15 ml tablespoon. Research 2026-11 (scratchpad report measures-research.md).

tsp_ml.note: Metric teaspoon. The US teaspoon is 4.93 ml (1.4% smaller), which does not matter here. Household cutlery spoons vary widely, so the site says 'measuring spoon'.

tbsp_ml.note: Metric tablespoon (UK, EU, US labeling). The Australian tablespoon is 20 ml, so only oil uses tablespoons; everything else is in teaspoons (5 ml everywhere).

spoon_step.note: Spoon amounts are rounded to the nearest 1/4 teaspoon or tablespoon. Common measuring spoon sets go down to 1/4 teaspoon; smaller names (pinch, dash) are not defined consistently.

spoon_min.note: Smallest spoon amount shown: 1/4 teaspoon (NIST table goes down to 1/4 tsp). Below that the column is empty: weigh, or use the yeast solution.

cube_step.note: Fresh yeast is shown as a fraction of the cube (yeast.solution.fresh.cube_g), rounded to the nearest 1/8. Judgment, not a measured value: cutting a cube by eye is about +/-30% for small pieces.

cube_min.note: Smallest cube fraction shown: 1/4 cube (about 10 g of a 42 g cube). Smaller pieces are eyeballing; then the column is empty and the reader weighs. No source gives a teaspoon value for fresh yeast (it is a compressible paste), so no spoons for fresh yeast.

flour.note: No cups for flour: a cup weighs 116-142 g depending on how it is filled (King Arthur 116-120 g, USDA 125 g, America's Test Kitchen 142 g), about 20%, which would move hydration by over 10 points. Grams only.

g_per_ml.note: Water density is 0.994-1.000 g/ml between 4 and 35 degrees C (under 0.6% off). The measuring jug's markings limit accuracy, not density.
Own calculation, not a looked-up value: a 1% dry or 3% fresh yeast solution is about 1.001-1.003 g/ml, under 0.5% from 1 g/ml. Stir before pouring; the yeast settles.

g_per_tsp.note: Fine table salt, level 5 ml teaspoon (USDA 6.0 g/tsp; King Arthur 18 g/tbsp; Milk Street weighing 6 g). Coarse, kosher and flaky salts weigh 2.8-5 g per teaspoon (Milk Street, labels, King Arthur), so the site tells readers to weigh coarse salt.
Granulated white sugar, level 5 ml teaspoon (USDA 4.2 g/tsp; King Arthur 198 g per cup = 4.2 g per 5 ml).
Olive oil density 0.91-0.92 g/ml (USDA 216 g per US cup; Canadian regulation B.09.003 relative density 0.910-0.916). 5 ml x 0.913 = 4.6 g. King Arthur's lower value (0.85 g/ml) is not used.

g_per_tbsp.note: 15 ml x 0.913 g/ml = 13.7 g (USDA 13.5 g per US tablespoon). Oil is shown in tablespoons from 1 tablespoon up, below that in teaspoons.

g_per_tsp.note: Instant dry yeast, level 5 ml teaspoon: King Arthur 2 1/4 tsp = 7 g; packet labels 7 g = about 2 1/4 tsp. USDA lists 4 g/tsp for active dry yeast, which contradicts its own 7.2 g packet = 1.8 tsp; not used. Granule size varies by brand (+/-10%).

yeast_fresh.note: Fresh yeast is shown as a fraction of the cube (yeast.solution.fresh.cube_g); no reliable teaspoon value exists.

yeast_pct_dry.note: 2 g per 300 g flour (0.667%). Typical straight-dough rule of thumb is 0.5-0.7% instant yeast (pizzamaking forum, secondhand); Reinhart NY about 0.71%. Sources vary up to 5x with fridge temperature and yeast brand. Treat as a starting point and adjust after baking. Validation review 2026-11 (m12): plausible at 26-28 C, at the low end for a 1.5-2x rise in 45-60 min; in a 21 C room it can take up to 90 min. See docs/test-bake-plan.md, item 1 (raise to about 0.8-1% if the rise takes more than 75 min at 26-28 C).

water_temp_c.note: Lukewarm. Yeast works well at 25-35 C and starts to die from about 50 C (validation m3; America's Test Kitchen: dies quickly at 54-60 C, risk above about 49 C).

knead_min.note: Value from the user's guide v7 (untested, no external source checked).

bulk_min.note: Bulk rise in a warm place (26-28 C), 45-60 min, until 1.5-2x. Planning uses the upper end. Validation review 2026-11 (M3): start heating the oven about halfway through this rise, so the baking surface is hot when the balls are ready; take the dough out first if it rises in the oven.

final_rest_min.note: Rest after dividing/balling (or in the pan), 30-45 min. Planning uses the upper end.

warm_2h.min_pizzas_note: 1 pizza needs under 1 g dry yeast (0.98 g at 30 cm) and the scale reads whole grams. Fresh yeast for 1 pizza would be about 2.2-3.3 g (weighable), but the user's rule (at least 2 pizzas for the warm method) is kept for both yeast types; the owner confirmed this rule after the validation (m4).

bulk_slow_max_min.note: Validation review 2026-11 (m12): without a warm place (about 21 C) the rise can take up to 90 minutes. Wait for the size, not the clock. Estimate, no source. See docs/test-bake-plan.md, item 1.

yeast_pct_dry.note: Only a home-recipe data point (0.3% overnight) and a forum reply ("no single right percentage") were found. May be too low. Sources vary up to 5x with fridge temperature and yeast brand. Treat as a starting point and adjust after baking. See docs/test-bake-plan.md, item 2.

water_temp_c.note: Cool water to slow the fermentation at room temperature. Estimate, not in the guide.

autolyse_min.note: Value from the user's guide v7 (untested, no external source checked).

knead_min.note: Value from the user's guide v7 (untested, no external source checked).

bulk_min.note: Planning assumption: about 4 h in bulk, then about 5 h in balls = 9 h at 21 C, inside the 8-12 h window. AVPN allows 8-24 h in total; the split is an estimate (Naples practice: bulk then balls).

final_rest_min.note: Time in balls (or in the pan) at room temperature.

yeast_pct_dry.note: ESTIMATE, interpolated between the 24 h and warm values; no source gives a 12-16 h figure. Lehmann (secondhand) quotes 0.375% for up to 3 days. Sources vary up to 5x with fridge temperature and yeast brand. Treat as a starting point and adjust after baking. See docs/test-bake-plan.md, item 3.

room_rest_min.note: Rest at 21 C for 1-1.5 h so the yeast starts, then divide, ball, fridge. Planning uses the lower end.

take_out_lead_min.note: Take the dough out of the fridge 1.5-2 h before baking (cold dough tears). Planning uses the upper end.

rounds.note: Three rounds of stretch and fold instead of kneading (guide v7). The guide also says 3-4 rounds. Done during the room-temperature rise: this site's reading of the guide, which did not say how the rounds and the 1-1.5 h rise fit together. Rounds at 0, 30 and 60 minutes; with stretch and fold the rise runs the full 90 minutes so the dough rests after the last round (validation m7).

practice._note: Numbers that appear in the New York step text. Most come from the user's guide v7 and are untested; values changed by the 2026-11 validation say so in their note. The pizza size is no longer here: the text refers to the size chosen on the Home page (validation M2; the guide's 30 cm was removed).

ball_g.note: AVPN allows 200-280 g, 22-35 cm. The site no longer states a fixed ball or size in the steps (validation M2): the Ingredients card shows the ball weight for the size chosen on the Home page (26, 30 or 32 cm = about 188, 250 or 284 g). The 32 cm ball is just over the AVPN maximum of 280 g (n5); the EU TSG reportedly gives 180-250 g (secondary).

dough_density_g_per_cm2.note: Derived from the user's guide v7 ball weight and diameter: 250 g for a 30 cm pizza = 250 / (pi x 15^2). Dough per pizza = pizza area x this density. AVPN allows 200-280 g for 22-35 cm for Neapolitan.

hydration.note: AVPN: 1600-1800 g flour per litre of water (about 56-63%). Home-oven sources use 65-76% because the bake is longer (America's Test Kitchen about 76%). AVPN numbers were read from the AVPN page by a summarizing tool; re-check the official PDF.

salt.note: AVPN 40-60 g per litre of water with 1.6-1.8 kg flour = about 2.2-3.75% of flour (validation n4 corrected the earlier '2.4-3.5%'); STG reportedly 50-55 g/L (secondary summary).

sugar.note: Optional, for colour at 250 C. America's Test Kitchen uses about 1.1%. Not part of the traditional recipe.

no_oil_no_sugar.note: The official EU specification for Pizza Napoletana (Commission Regulation (EU) No 97/2010, Traditional Speciality Guaranteed) lists only flour, water, salt and yeast for the dough; olive oil is used only on top (validation m10). The AVPN page lists no forbidden ingredients. Not re-read by a person for this site (the validator read it; a re-fetch during the fix failed), so verified stays false.

temp_c.note: Home oven maximum. A real Neapolitan oven runs 430-480 C for 60-90 s (AVPN).

time_min.note: Vendor/blog sources say 5-7 min with the broiler at the end; add about 1 min if the oven is cooler than 290 C (America's Test Kitchen).

last_min.note: Bake with top+bottom heat, then switch on the grill for the last 1-2 minutes. Never more than 3-5 minutes of grill in total.

max_min.note: America's Test Kitchen broils 4-5 min at 550 F on a hotter steel.

avpn_oven_c.note: AVPN rule, read from the AVPN page by a summarizing tool; re-check the official disciplinare. A real Neapolitan wood oven.

avpn_bake_s.note: AVPN rule, read from the AVPN page by a summarizing tool; re-check the official disciplinare. Bake time in the 430-480 C oven.

avpn_ferment_h.note: AVPN rule, read from the AVPN page by a summarizing tool; re-check the official disciplinare. Minimum 8 h, maximum 24 h; temperature not set (room temperature in Naples practice).

avpn_rim_cm.note: AVPN rule, read from the AVPN page by a summarizing tool; re-check the official disciplinare. Rim (cornicione) 1-2 cm.

avpn_diameter_cm.note: AVPN rule, read from the AVPN page by a summarizing tool; re-check the official disciplinare. Pizza diameter up to 35 cm (secondary sources).

home_hydration_pct.note: Home-oven recipes use more water than the AVPN range because the bake is longer (America's Test Kitchen about 76%). Blog and test-kitchen sources.

practice._note: Numbers that appear in the Neapolitan text and are not elsewhere in this file. Other numbers of that text reuse styles.new_york.practice. The guide's 28-30 cm shaping size was removed (validation M2): the text refers to the size chosen on the Home page.
